verdict: Moderna lost $782M in its quiet season — revenue of just $145M cannot cover $651M of research — but the loss narrowed from a year ago as costs fell, and management improved its full-year expense and cash outlook.

kpis.label: R&D spending
kpis.note: -7% YoY as late-stage trials wind down

segments.name: Net product sales
segments.note: Vaccine sales — mainly COVID vaccines. Sales fell in the U.S. and South America, partly offset by deliveries in the U.K. under a long-term government partnership. Revenue was $87M in the U.S. and $58M international (including other revenue).

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Grants, collaborations, licensing and royalties — and this quarter, stand-ready manufacturing revenue, which is why this line nearly doubled.

flow.costPlain: Making vaccines in plants that run far below capacity in the off-season — including $41M of inventory write-downs and $23M of unutilized manufacturing capacity costs.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: The labs: developing new vaccines and drugs. Down 7% — several late-stage programs wound down, plus deliberate cost cuts.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, offices, admin. Down 6% — the company is holding this line down too.

otherDetail: Interest income of $67M, less $19M of other expense — net $48M.
footerNote: Q2 is Moderna's seasonal trough quarter.
pngFooterNote: Q2 is Moderna's seasonal trough quarter.
follow100Note: For every $100 of revenue, Moderna spent $449 on research alone — Q2 revenue is a trickle, but the labs run all year. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The trough quarter, by design
takeaways.text: Moderna's year is back-loaded: fall vaccination drives the second half, and about 55% of second-half revenue is expected in Q3 alone. Q2's $145M — $87M of it in the U.S. — is the smallest quarter of the year, against $867M of research and overhead.

takeaways.title: Costs are coming down
takeaways.text: R&D fell 7% to $651M, SG&A 6% to $216M and cost of sales 22% to $93M. Moderna improved its 2026 operating-expense outlook by about $0.2B and raised its expected year-end cash to $4.7–5.2B.

takeaways.title: The pipeline giveth and taketh away
takeaways.text: The norovirus vaccine's Phase 3 interim analysis missed its early-success criteria, so Moderna will enroll an additional cohort. Offsetting that: its flu vaccine mFLUSIVA faced an August 5 FDA decision date, and Phase 3 melanoma data for the intismeran cancer vaccine could arrive in 2026.

oneTimers: Cost of sales includes $41M of inventory write-downs and $23M of costs for manufacturing capacity that sat unused — the price of keeping vaccine plants ready for the fall season.

After the quarter ended, Moderna paid $950M in July 2026 to settle the litigation announced in Q1 — the settlement behind a roughly $0.9B non-recurring charge in first-half cost of sales (first-half cost of sales was $1,048M, vs $209M a year ago). That payment is not in Q2's $93M.
